Welcome to Pebble Brook
Pebble Brook School is a special school located in Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire.
Pebble Brook caters for children and young people with special educational needs, supporting a wide range of learning, communication and developmental needs through a personalised and nurturing approach.
Find out more about our students, staff and Pebble Brook School’s mission and values.
Our Curriculum
We aim to prepare students for life beyond school.
We support students to become active, responsible and valued members of their community.
We are preparing our students not just for the next stage of education, but life beyond the classroom.

Safeguarding
Safeguarding
Safeguarding at Pebble Brook School is highly effective and deeply embedded in our culture. The safety, dignity and wellbeing of every student is at the heart of everything we do.
We recognise the additional vulnerabilities of our students and take a proactive, vigilant and uncompromising approach to safeguarding. Pupils are known exceptionally well as individuals, and staff work tirelessly to ensure they feel safe, secure and valued.
Our safeguarding approach
We recognise that pupils at Pebble Brook may be more vulnerable due to additional needs, communication differences, or past experiences. Our safeguarding arrangements are therefore robust, proactive, and tailored to meet the specific needs of our pupils.
Receive regular safeguarding and child protection training
Understand their duty to act immediately on any concern
Are trained to recognise signs of abuse, neglect, exploitation, mental health concerns or any other sign of concerns
Safeguarding procedures follow current statutory guidance, including Keeping Children Safe in Education, and are reviewed regularly.
Safeguarding leadership
Safeguarding is led by experienced Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL), supported by trained deputy DSLs. Together, they ensure that safeguarding arrangements are:
Leadership maintains a clear oversight of safeguarding practice, ensuring timely action and robust accountability.
Consistently implemented across the school
Responsive to emerging needs and risks
Understood and applied by all staff
A strong culture of vigilance
There is a pervasive culture of safeguarding vigilance across the school.
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility, and this is clearly understood by all members of the school community.
Working in partnership
We work with parents, carers and external agencies to safeguard pupils.
Strong partnerships with:
Ensure that pupils and their families receive timely, coordinated and effective support.
Referrals from school are swift, appropriate, and well-informed, reflecting a strong understanding of safeguarding processes.
Social care
Health professionals
The local authority
Safer recruitment & staff development
We take a rigorous and uncompromising approach to safer recruitment.
As a result, staff are knowledgeable, confident, and highly vigilant.
Supporting pupils wellbeing
Pupils’ wellbeing is prioritised and actively promoted.
All support is carefully tailored to meet pupils’ individual needs, ensuring no child or young person is overlooked.
Recruitment processes follow best practice guidance
Online safety
Online safety is given a high priority.
Policies and Practice
Our safeguarding practice is firmly rooted in statutory guidance, including Keeping Children Safe in Education, and is reflected in our comprehensive policies.
Key policies include:
These are regularly reviewed, implemented, and consistently followed, ensuring that practice remains strong and effective.
We encourage all members of the community to act if they have any concerns.

About us
At Pebble Brook School
Our ethos is shaped by the belief that every student is unique and deserves the opportunity to thrive academically, socially and personally.
We provide a nurturing, inclusive environment where students feel safe, valued, and understood, enabling them to reach their full potential. This reflects the school’s longstanding emphasis on individuality and supporting students to maximise their independence and future readiness.
Our vision
To prepare every student for a fulfilling future by nurturing their abilities, promoting their wellbeing, building their confidence, and empowering them to take their next steps with pride.
Our curriculum is carefully designed to support each young person’s journey into adulthood, with a strong focus on communication, literacy, numeracy, life skills, social development, emotional wellbeing, and independence.
We must respect everyone and their belongings and keep our classroom clean
We try our best in everything, we can do it!
Resilience
Keep going when things get challenging, every step brings you closer to success
Support one another and work as a team to reach our goals
Integrity
Tell the truth and take responsibility for your actions
Include everyone and celebrate our differences
We model and promote respect for ourselves, one another, and our school community. Positive relationships underpin learning and help create a calm, supportive environment.
We encourage all students to recognise their strengths, celebrate progress, and strive for their personal best in every area of school life. High expectations help every child move forward with confidence.
We help students develop emotional strength, problem solving skills, and a belief that effort leads to progress. Supporting emotional regulation and coping strategies is central to our work with our learners.
We value teamwork and strong partnerships—between students, staff, families, and the wider community. We are committed to create initiatives that exemplify meaningful opportunities for students to learn through real life collaboration.
We teach and expect honesty, responsibility, fairness, and doing the right thing even when it is difficult. Integrity supports students in becoming trustworthy, thoughtful young adults.
We are proud to be a community special school where every student belongs. Our provision recognises and supports diverse needs within an environment that celebrates individuality.

Ofsted
Ofsted Inspection
Pebble Brook School Churchill Avenue, Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire HP21 8LZ
Inspection dates: 13 to 14 March 2024
Outcome
Pebble Brook School continues to be a good school.
What is it like to attend this school?
Pupils at Pebble Brook School thrive. They have exceptionally positive attitudes to learning and work hard to achieve their very best. From the moment they start at the school, the focus is on preparing for a successful future.
Pupils are provided with rich experiences which inspire them. They are motivated to work hard to achieve their aspirations. Parents particularly value the support on offer with one explaining to inspectors how well their child is being supported to ‘reach their full potential at this school’. There is a distinctly inclusive and nurturing ethos throughout the school.
Staff know pupils very well. This is evident in the strong relationships between staff and pupils. This carries through to equally respectful and kind interactions between pupils. Pupils are well supported to grow their confidence. They appreciate the guidance they receive to manage their own emotional wellbeing. They learn strategies to self-regulate. As a result, a consistently calm and purposeful atmosphere permeates the school.
Pupils feel safe and secure here. They are taught to understand that everyone is different. They are accepted and able to be themselves. Pupils in the sixth form are kind and helpful. They are strong role models for the younger pupils to look up to

Welcome
Welcome to the Pebble Brook
We are an inclusive, forward‑looking secondary school serving our local community, where young people are known, challenged, and supported to succeed. Everything we do is rooted in our core values of respect, aspiration, resilience, collaboration, integrity, and inclusivity.
These values shape our expectations, guide our relationships, and underpin our commitment to helping every pupil grow into a confident, capable, and responsible individual.
Students at Pebble Brook School have a range of special educational needs and disabilities, including Cognition and Learning needs, Autistic Spectrum Condition and Speech and Language needs. All students have an Education, Health and Social Care plan which sets out the additional support required to meet their needs.
At Pebble Brook, pupils are at the heart of every decision we make. We create a purposeful learning environment through carefully planned curriculum, strong classroom practice, clear routines, and consistently high expectations. Teachers work collaboratively to deliver engaging lessons, assess progress carefully, and provide timely academic intervention where needed. Alongside this, our pastoral systems ensure that pupils receive structured guidance, mentoring, and emotional support, helping them to develop resilience, independence, and confidence as learners and as young people.
Positive relationships across our school are built through daily practice, not words alone. Staff take time to know pupils well, model respect and integrity, and set clear boundaries within an inclusive and supportive culture. We value working closely with families, encouraging open communication and shared responsibility for pupils’ progress and wellbeing. Collaboration—between staff, pupils, parents, and external partners—plays a key role in ensuring that every young person feels a strong sense of belonging and is supported to achieve highly.
This website offers an insight into life at Pebble Brook School. You will find information about our curriculum and enrichment programme, key policies, our school calendar, staff team, and guidance for families. It is designed to help you understand how our school operates and the opportunities available to our pupils, both in and beyond the classroom.
If you are considering Pebble Brook for your child, are interested in working with us, or would like to explore partnership opportunities, we warmly encourage you to get in touch or attend one of our open events. Our school thrives on strong relationships and shared ambition, and we look forward to welcoming you into our community.
Yours sincerely, Susanna Sutton Headteacher

Pastoral Support
Pastoral Support
At Pebble Brook School, we place a strong emphasis on the pastoral care of our students, recognising that emotional wellbeing is fundamental to learning and development. All staff are trained in trauma-informed practice, ensuring that every interaction is supportive, understanding, and responsive to individual need.
Our dedicated pastoral team of four staff members acts as a vital link between school and home. They work closely with families to provide consistent support, build strong relationships, and ensure that students feel safe and understood.
Mental Health
We also have trained Mental Health First Aiders within our staff, alongside team members who have received specialist bereavement training. This enables us to offer sensitive and informed support during times of difficulty.
We collaborate with a range of external agencies, including Buckinghamshire CAMHS, to ensure that students and families can access additional expertise when needed.
We are committed to working in partnership with our families and always welcome communication. At Pebble Brook, every member of staff is dedicated to supporting students not only in their academic progress but also in their emotional wellbeing.

School Uniform
School Uniform Policy
At Pebble Brook School, our uniform policy has been developed in partnership with our young people. We believe that a simple, comfortable, and practical uniform helps to reduce barriers to learning, and supports pupils to feel confident and ready for school each day.
Our approach to uniform is rooted in respect, inclusivity, and individual choice while maintaining clear and consistent expectations.
Pupils are expected to wear:
We have worked together with pupils to make these Golden Rules for school.
White polo shirt or plain white T‑shirt
Black trousers or black joggers
This uniform has been chosen to allow flexibility, comfort, and ease of movement, supporting pupils to engage fully in learning throughout the day. Some pupils choose to wear blazers and ties. These are not compulsory, and pupils may decide whether this option works best for them.
Sixth form dress code
Sixth Form students are not required to wear school uniform and may wear their own clothing. Clothing should be appropriate for a school environment, supporting a professional and respectful atmosphere and setting a positive example to younger pupils.
Our Expectations
All uniform and clothing should be:
We work constructively and sensitively with pupils and families if uniform concerns arise, ensuring that expectations are clear and support is provided where needed.
Our uniform policy reflects Pebble Brook’s commitment to supporting learning, promoting equality, and listening to the voices of our young people. Full details can be found in our Uniform Policy, available on this website.
If you have any questions or need support regarding uniform, please contact the school and a member of staff will be happy to help.
